correctness.rationale: The pmf difference follows exactly from the three coefficients of a fixed-sum Bernoulli pair. Its generating polynomial is (z-1)^2 times the Poisson-binomial background polynomial, which is real-rooted with no positive roots; the real-rooted Descartes lemma gives exactly two coefficient sign changes. Telescoping and unimodality then yield the CDF and W1 identities, while TV, Kolmogorov, and stop-loss are direct exact consequences. The embedded rational checker replays all formulas.

originality.rationale: Hoeffding covers the qualitative convex-order effect and finite-difference expectation machinery; that part is explicitly not treated as original. Wang covers Poisson-binomial unimodality and Roos covers finite-difference binomial approximation. The inspected and searched sources do not state or dominate the exact two-crossing pmf law together with the one-crossing CDF and closed TV/Kolmogorov/W1/stop-loss transfer formulas.
residual_risks: Classical total-positivity or Pólya-frequency literature may encode an equivalent two-crossing result without Poisson-binomial terminology.

The exact finite-difference identity itself is closely related to Hoeffding's classical pair-variation algebra; originality rests on the combined crossing and metric classification, not on the raw convolution identity alone.

value.rationale: A pair-balancing T-transform is the atomic operation behind majorization of Bernoulli parameter vectors. The theorem quantifies that atomic operation completely at the distribution level: a single central depletion band, two tail gains, one CDF crossing, exact metric costs, and a threshold-by-threshold stop-loss increment. The W1 coefficient is the modal mass of the remaining Bernoulli sum, connecting transport sensitivity directly to concentration.
